explanation: In chronological order the cases run Alipore conspiracy (1908), Howrah-Dacca conspiracies (1910), Kakori case (1925), then the Central Assembly Bomb Case (1929) -- i.e. II, IV, I, III.
Each term is half the previous one (2, 1, 1/2, 1/4...), so the next term is 1/8. Note 2/8 equals 1/4, the previous term, making it a trap.
The series alternates +1 then +3 (3→4→7→8→11→12), so after 12 the next step is +3, giving 15.
Each term is multiplied by an increasing factor: ×2, ×3, ×4, so the next multiplier is ×5, giving 72×5 = 360.
This is a Fibonacci-style series where each term is the sum of the two before it (3+5=8), so the next term is 5+8 = 13.
The differences between consecutive terms decrease by 2 each time (21, 19, 17, 15...), so the next difference is 13, giving 48-13 = 35.
Each term is 5 times a perfect square (5×1², 5×2², 5×3², 5×4²), so the next term is 5×5² = 125.
11, 13 and 17 are prime numbers, while 15 (=3×5) is not, making 15 the odd one out.
144, 196 and 256 are perfect squares (12², 14², 16²), while 168 is not, making it the odd one out.
If n friends originally planned to share Rs. 96, and 4 dropped out raising each remaining share by Rs. 4, solving 96/(n-4) - 96/n = 4 gives n = 12, so 12-4 = 8 friends actually attended.
